stem.en: Which gold foil result could Thomson's model not explain at all?

text.en: A few alpha particles bounced almost straight back, because charge spread over a whole atom is too weak to turn a fast particle around.
Most alpha particles passed straight through, because Thomson's atom is a solid ball that should have stopped them.
Some alpha particles bent a little, because Thomson's model says a particle can never bend at all.

explanation.en: Thomson's atom is not a hard ball: its charge is spread thinly, so the model expects particles to pass through and to bend a little. That rules out the second and third options. What it cannot give is a push strong enough to send a fast particle back. Only positive charge packed into one tiny place can do that.

hints.en: Think about what Thomson's model expected before the experiment. Which result is far outside that?
